title: Landlord screening by months of on-time rent transfers
moment: A tenant in Taipei applies for a rental flat and the landlord or agent asks for bank statements to judge whether the tenant reliably pays rent on time.
verifier: Landlord or rental agency (e.g. a property agent handling the lease)
predicate: Count of months in the last 12 in which a rent-sized recurring transfer (at or above a stated amount) was made on or before the due day is at least 11
disclosed_today: Several months of full bank statements or passbook photocopies, showing every merchant, salary source, medical payment and balance.
issuer: The tenant's bank, signing a statistic computed from its own transaction ledger
why_zk: A bank-signed count of on-time recurring payments answers the landlord's real question without exposing the rest of the statement. Weak points are that no Taiwan bank issues such a signed statistic today, landlords have little leverage to demand a wallet proof, and rent is often paid in cash or to a different account, so coverage would be partial.

title: Cram school or kindergarten fee-installment eligibility from average monthly balance
moment: A parent enrolling a child in a private kindergarten, cram school or bilingual programme asks for a multi-month instalment plan, and the school wants reassurance the parent can sustain the payments.
verifier: Private school or cram school finance office
predicate: Average daily balance across all the parent's accounts at the bank over the last 6 months is at least a threshold equal to the remaining tuition
disclosed_today: Photocopy of the passbook or bank statements, or a post-dated cheque plus a guarantor's details, revealing balances, counterparties and sometimes the guarantor's identity.
issuer: The parent's bank, signing an average-balance statistic over the accounts held there
why_zk: An average-balance threshold is far less than a full statement, and it avoids pulling in a guarantor. Honestly weak because many schools simply use post-dated cheques or credit-card auto-billing, which already settle the risk, and a single bank's aggregate misses balances held elsewhere, so the school may not accept it as sufficient.

title: Small-claims or maintenance negotiation proving total outflow to one payee
moment: In a mediation at a township mediation committee or a family-court conciliation, one party says they have paid the other a certain total (for example support or a loan repayment) over a year, and the other side disputes the sum.
verifier: Mediator, court clerk or the counterparty's lawyer
predicate: Sum of transfers from the person's account to a named payee account between two dates equals or exceeds a stated amount
disclosed_today: Printed or screenshotted full account statements for the period, exposing every unrelated transaction, which are often partly blacked out by hand and then questioned for authenticity.
issuer: The bank holding the paying account, signing a sum over a filtered set of transactions
why_zk: A bank-signed total to a single named payee is verifiable and removes hand redaction and doubts about doctored screenshots. Honest limits are that courts in Taiwan currently accept bank-issued certificates and discovery orders rather than cryptographic proofs, so this is most plausible as an informal mediation aid, and the payee identity is itself disclosed by the predicate.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Limit what is released to what the stated purpose needs, here a payment-regularity count, but with a proof instead of the holder's judgment.
Strip the identifying fields (payees, amounts, other counterparties) and keep only the derived figure.

title: Landlord checks six months of rent payments without seeing the bank statement
moment: A tenant renewing or applying for a rental in Taipei or Taichung is asked by the landlord or agent to photograph passbook pages or send bank statements to prove they have always paid rent on time.
verifier: Landlord or rental agency
predicate: Count of monthly outgoing transfers of at least the rent amount to the same payee in the last 6 months is 6, with no more than 0 returned or failed transfers.
disclosed_today: Full statements or passbook pages showing every transaction, balances, employer name, medical or religious payees, and family transfers.
issuer: Tenant's bank (bank signs the count over its own transaction ledger)
why_zk: The bank already holds the ledger and can sign a count with the rule stated. Weakness is that the landlord cannot tell whether the tenant paid from several accounts, and cash or other-bank rent is invisible, so the proof covers only one bank. The tenant can choose which account to prove, which biases the result. Landlord practice in Taiwan also leans on guarantors and deposits, so the proof only replaces the statement, not the deposit.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A published aggregate can still reveal individual contributors, so the threshold and rounding of the signed statistic must be chosen with that leak in mind.
Release only the aggregate and never an output that lets a particular counterparty be singled out.

title: Micro-business owner proves quarterly card-sales turnover to a landlord or platform without exposing customers
moment: A night-market stall or small shop owner applying for a stall lease, a delivery-platform onboarding, or a government small-business subsidy is asked for bank statements of the business account to show monthly sales volume.
verifier: Market management office, platform, or subsidy-handling agency
predicate: Sum of incoming mobile-payment and card-settlement deposits over the last 3 months is at least a stated threshold, and the number of distinct payers exceeds a stated minimum.
disclosed_today: Complete business account statements listing every customer transfer, supplier payment, personal withdrawals and balances.
issuer: Bank holding the business account, as merchant acquirer or account holder
why_zk: A signed sum and distinct-payer count answers the real question (is this a live business) and hides suppliers and customers. Honest limits: much night-market revenue is cash and never reaches the bank, so the proof understates, and the tax authority, not the bank, is the usual authority on turnover. Distinct-payer counts can also leak small-group membership if the threshold is low, which differential-privacy style thinking warns about.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Purpose-limited release of only the figure the programme needs, replacing reliance on the verifier's promise.
The holder discloses one derived attribute from a larger record instead of handing over the whole record.
A verifier asking for broad statements when it needs one narrow scope, and the issuer being free to sign only the narrow one.

title: Insurer or employer wellness program checks monthly gym and pharmacy spending band, not itemized purchases
moment: A health-insurance discount programme or a corporate wellness benefit in Taiwan asks participants to upload credit-card statements to prove they spent on fitness, with the same statements revealing pharmacy, clinic and other purchases.
verifier: Private insurer or employer benefits administrator
predicate: Total card spending in merchant categories for gyms and sports venues over 12 months falls in a stated band, computed by the bank over the cardholder's cards, with no other category disclosed.
disclosed_today: Itemized card statements across all merchants, showing health, pharmacy, entertainment and location patterns.
issuer: Card-issuing bank, which categorizes transactions by merchant category code
why_zk: The bank can sign a category aggregate across the person's cards at the same bank. Weak points: merchant category codes are coarse and gameable, cards at other banks are missing, and a verifier that asks for a narrow band can still infer health status from participation, so the aggregate itself is sensitive. Personal Data Protection Act purpose limitation already pushes toward minimal collection, but nothing proves the minimal set was what was collected.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a private party asking for full copies of documents when a narrow fact would do, with no less-intrusive alternative named.
A payment-related check that escalates into collecting extra personal documents beyond what the purpose needs.

title: Landlord checks rent-payment regularity without seeing the tenant's bank statement
moment: A tenant applying for a rental in Taipei is asked by the landlord or agent to send photos of 6 to 12 months of passbook or e-banking statements to show they pay rent on time and have a steady balance.
verifier: Private landlord or rental agency (房仲)
predicate: In each of the last 12 months, the account made a recurring transfer of at least NT$X to a rent-like payee on or before the due date, and the month-end balance never fell below one month's rent.
disclosed_today: Full statements showing every transaction, counterparties, merchants, medical or family payments, salary source, and account number.
issuer: The tenant's bank, signing a payment-regularity and minimum-balance aggregate over the account's transactions.
why_zk: The landlord needs only a yes/no on regularity and buffer, and a bank-signed aggregate proves it without the transaction list. Weakness: there is no standard for such a bank attestation today, and private landlords may not accept anything but the familiar statement photos. The tenant may also rent from several accounts, so the claim covers only one account.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Demanding extra records from a user whose payments are already normal, without stating necessity.
Concern that data collected for onboarding gets retained under an open-ended business-need exception, which pushes towards proving a band instead of handing over records.

title: Night-market stall applies for a platform seller badge with a turnover band, not account history
moment: A small food or goods vendor applying to sell through a delivery or e-commerce platform in Taiwan is asked to upload bank statements to show monthly receipts, so the platform can set a deposit or credit limit.
verifier: Delivery or e-commerce platform's merchant onboarding team
predicate: Total incoming deposits across the vendor's business accounts over the last 6 months fall in a stated band (for example NT$100,000 to NT$300,000 per month), and no month is more than 30 percent below the average.
disclosed_today: Complete statements for personal and business accounts, including customer names on transfers, private spending, and family transfers, often mixed in the same account.
issuer: The vendor's bank (including a credit cooperative or farmers' and fishermen's association bank), signing a turnover-band aggregate.
why_zk: The platform needs a turnover band to set a limit, not the customer-level detail. The bank can sign the band over all the vendor's accounts at that bank. Weakness: many stall owners mix cash and informal transfers, so bank deposits understate real turnover and the band may be unfairly low. Banks would also have to build and support the attestation product.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A cross-border intermediary requiring full ID or document copies with no lighter alternative stated.
Bundles of identity and financial document copies requested when a narrower check could satisfy the purpose.

title: Overseas-study sponsor shows enough funds without handing a school the family's whole account history
moment: A Taiwanese family applying for a student visa or university admission abroad must show a parent's bank statements proving funds for tuition and living costs for the first year, and the parent sends months of statements to a foreign admissions office or visa agent.
verifier: Foreign university admissions office, embassy, or study-abroad agency in Taiwan
predicate: The sponsor's combined balance across the bank's accounts has stayed at or above the required amount (for example NT$1,000,000) for each of the last 90 days.
disclosed_today: Full statements and sometimes a copy of the national ID, revealing the family's spending, other relatives' transfers, employer, and exact balances well above the threshold.
issuer: The sponsor's bank, signing a minimum-balance-over-period aggregate across the sponsor's accounts at that bank.
why_zk: Only a threshold held over a period matters, and the exact balance and history stay hidden. A bank-signed aggregate also helps against doctored statements. Weakness: foreign institutions set their own formats and will rarely accept a Taiwan wallet proof, so uptake depends on the receiving side, and an agent in the middle often insists on seeing paper statements.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a verifier demanding an ID and extra documents to confirm one payment fact, with no stated purpose or less intrusive alternative.
The idea that the holder must release only what serves the purpose, but needs a mechanism that proves the released subset is minimal.

title: Landlord rent-payment track record without sharing the tenant's bank statements
moment: A tenant renewing a lease or applying for a new rental in Taipei is asked by the landlord or agent to hand over several months of passbook pages or bank app screenshots to show they pay rent on time.
verifier: Private landlord or rental agency (房仲/包租代管業者)
predicate: Over the last 12 months, at least 11 monthly outgoing transfers to the same payee were made on or before the 5th of the month (count and on-time ratio computed by the bank).
disclosed_today: Full passbook or app screenshots showing every transaction, balances, salary source, merchants, other account numbers, and often the ID card copy.
issuer: The tenant's bank (signing a payment-regularity statistic over the account's transfers)
why_zk: The landlord only needs on-time rent history, not the tenant's whole financial life. Weak spot: the bank would need to define and sign a payment-regularity statistic and tie it to a payee, which no Taiwanese bank offers today, and landlords may still prefer an ID copy and guarantor regardless. Still, the over-collection of statements is real and the aggregate is much smaller.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A small registration fact does not justify copying the whole document; record only the fields the rule requires.
Release only the subset that serves the stated purpose.

title: Proving a stable monthly foreign-remittance pattern to a migrant worker's home-country sponsor or broker
moment: A migrant worker in Taiwan, or the Taiwanese employer or broker, is asked by a recruitment agency, a visa-renewal service or a home-country lender to show the worker regularly sends money home, and the agency collects full remittance receipts and bank statements.
verifier: Recruitment broker (仲介), home-country microfinance lender, or family-visit visa service
predicate: Total remitted abroad in the last 6 months is at least NT$X and remittances occurred in at least 5 of 6 months.
disclosed_today: Complete bank statements and remittance slips including employer salary details, deductions, beneficiary names, and sometimes a passport copy.
issuer: The worker's bank or remittance-licensed bank (signing a sum and count over transfers)
why_zk: The verifier needs a regularity and amount signal, not the beneficiary list or salary breakdown. Honest caveat: brokers often have commercial reasons to see more (wage deductions, debt), and a worker with weak bargaining power may be pressed to disclose anyway, so a proof helps only if the verifier agrees to accept it.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Collected data tends to be kept under a vague 'needed for business' exception, which a proof avoids by never handing over the records.
A request category that bundles extra fields with the one fact wanted; here the statement bundles customer detail with the revenue band.

title: Merchant proving monthly card-sales volume for a terminal or subsidy eligibility without exposing customers' transactions
moment: A night-market stall owner or small shop applying for a mobile-payment terminal upgrade, a municipal small-business subsidy or a supplier credit line is asked for twelve months of acquiring-bank settlement records, which list every customer card transaction.
verifier: Local government economic development bureau, payment processor, or wholesale supplier offering trade credit
predicate: Average monthly card and mobile-payment settlement over the last 12 months is between NT$A and NT$B, with no month below NT$C.
disclosed_today: Full settlement statements with per-transaction timestamps, amounts, masked card numbers, and the shop's account balances and bank transfers.
issuer: The merchant's acquiring or settlement bank (signing a sales aggregate)
why_zk: The verifier only needs a revenue band. Per-transaction detail also exposes customers' purchasing patterns that the merchant has no business passing on. Weakness: many subsidies already rely on tax filings (營業稅申報) that the government can check directly, so the case is strongest for private verifiers such as suppliers and processors.

title: Night-market stall helper proves current employment to get a staff-only phone plan or rental viewing slot
moment: A landlord or agency in Taipei offers a lower rent or fast-track viewing to tenants who are currently employed at a stable company, and asks for a recent pay slip or employment certificate.
verifier: Private landlord or rental agency
predicate: Holder is currently employed by a registered employer (not terminated or resigned) as of the last 24 hours
disclosed_today: Employment certificate or pay slip showing full name, national ID number, salary, employer, job title, address
issuer: The employer, via an employer-signed credential with revocation upon termination
why_zk: Landlords only need "still employed now", yet receive salary and ID number and can keep copies. A static certificate cannot show it is still true; a fresh proof with revocation can. Weak points in practice are that few employers issue wallet credentials, small employers may not run revocation infrastructure, and landlords may still want salary level for rent-to-income judgment, which this does not provide.

title: Contract cleaner or security guard proves current on-duty authorization at a building gate
moment: A building management office or gated community in Taiwan lets outsourced staff (cleaning, security, delivery of company goods) enter when their employer vouches they are currently on its roster, and today collects an ID copy and writes down the national ID number in a paper visitor log.
verifier: Building management committee or reception desk
predicate: Holder is on the active roster of a named contractor employer as of now
disclosed_today: National ID card photocopy or recorded ID number, full name, phone number, plus a paper letter from the contractor
issuer: The contracting employer, signing a short-lived roster-membership credential and revoking it when the worker leaves
why_zk: The building needs only "this person is currently sent by this company", but keeps ID numbers in logbooks that are easily leaked. Revocation matters because ex-employees keep old letters. Weakness is that the verifier often also wants to know the individual's name for accountability, so the unlinkable version may conflict with building security rules.

title: Gig courier proves current platform affiliation to access a company mailroom or campus dock
moment: A delivery rider arrives at a science-park company mailroom or hospital loading dock that only admits couriers currently contracted with a recognized logistics platform, and staff ask to see a worker card and ID.
verifier: Science park, hospital or corporate mailroom security
predicate: Rider is currently active and in good standing with a named logistics employer as of now
disclosed_today: Worker card, national ID or driver licence shown or photographed, name, phone number, vehicle plate
issuer: The logistics employer or platform operator, with revocation upon contract end or suspension
why_zk: The gatekeeper needs only current standing, but collects identity details of many people who visit daily. A fresh signed status also stops a suspended rider from using a stale card. Honest caveat is that many couriers are legally independent contractors rather than employees, so the platform may not count as an employer, and sites often want a plate or name for incident tracing.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Monthly re-presentation of a proof of prior authorisation without becoming a persistent identifier.
Sharing only the single employment-status attribute from a larger HR record.

title: Currently-employed proof for the convenience-store parcel pickup of a company-paid corporate card
moment: A new hire at a Hsinchu science-park firm opens a corporate-sponsored e-commerce or transit-subsidy account that is only valid while the person is employed, and the platform must re-confirm every month that the employment has not ended.
verifier: Corporate benefits platform or commuter-shuttle/subsidy operator that serves many employers
predicate: Holder is currently employed by a firm enrolled in the programme, as attested within the last 30 days, and the attestation has not been revoked.
disclosed_today: Employee ID, full name, department, job title, employer HR letter or staff card photo, sometimes payroll slip.
issuer: Employer HR system (signs a short-lived employment-active credential and revokes it on resignation).
why_zk: The platform only needs 'still employed at an enrolled firm', but today collects a full HR letter that identifies the person and role. A short-lived unlinkable proof with revocation fits well. Weakness: the employer must run an issuance and revocation service, and small firms may not; the platform may also want a stable account key, so unlinkability across months is partly given up by design.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Redemption that cannot be linked across uses, so repeated meals do not build a visit log.

title: Active-staff proof for staff-only discount at a hospital or university cafeteria and parking
moment: A nurse or contract cleaner at a hospital in Taichung wants the staff meal rate and staff parking tariff, which operators run via outsourced concessions that must not give staff rates to people who have left.
verifier: Outsourced cafeteria or parking concessionaire
predicate: Holder is on the active payroll or roster of this institution as of today (freshness under 24 hours).
disclosed_today: Staff card with name, photo and employee number, which the cashier or parking system logs and may keep.
issuer: Hospital or university HR/outsourcing employer, including the contractor employer for outsourced workers.
why_zk: The concessionaire needs only 'currently on staff', yet logs identity-bearing cards, creating a record of when each worker eats and parks. A daily-refreshed credential with revocation lets leavers drop off the same day. Weakness: staff discounts are often tied to a name for billing or payroll deduction, in which case identity is legitimately needed; the privacy gain is real only for cash or point-of-sale discounts.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The signing agency certifies status without being able to link the later presentation back to the issuance event.
A yes/no fact proven in a device-bound way so neither the issuer nor the verifier can track the holder.

title: Still-employed check on gig-platform or staffing-agency workers entering a client factory gate
moment: A dispatched worker from a staffing agency arrives at a client's plant in Taoyuan; the gate must confirm that the agency still employs them, since dispatch contracts end abruptly.
verifier: Client factory security gate or contractor-access system
predicate: Holder is currently employed by a named staffing agency under a live dispatch contract, with the signature issued today and revocable.
disclosed_today: National ID card copy or number, full name, phone number, agency contract copy, entered into a visitor log.
issuer: Staffing or dispatch agency as employer.
why_zk: The gate needs a fresh yes/no on 'currently dispatched by agency X', but collects ID numbers that are retained in paper logs. A freshness proof removes the ID collection. Weakness: workplace safety and labour-dispatch rules may require named records of who was on site (for incident and insurance reasons), so the plant may be legally obliged to keep identity; zero-knowledge here only covers the entry check, not the safety register.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a private party asking for full document copies at contract signing when a narrow check would serve the purpose.

title: Still-employed proof for a landlord's mid-lease rent-guarantee renewal
moment: A tenant in Taipei renews a one-year lease, and the landlord's agent asks again for a recent employment certificate, payslip and ID copy to confirm the tenant still has a job, even though the original paperwork was collected at signing.
verifier: Landlord or rental agency (房東 / 租賃仲介)
predicate: Tenant is currently employed by a registered employer (not terminated or resigned) as of today, with no employer name, salary or ID number revealed.
disclosed_today: Full ID copy, payslips showing salary and employer, employment certificate with company name, title and start date.
issuer: The employer's HR system, which signs a short-lived 'active employee' status and revokes it on termination or resignation.
why_zk: Freshness is the whole point: an old certificate cannot show the person is still employed, so a signed status with revocation is stronger than paper. The landlord only needs a yes about current employment. Practice is weak because landlords often want salary level too, and small employers may not run a wallet-capable HR system, so adoption depends on the employer side.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A telco check that relies on copyable identifiers and so cannot show current, genuine status.
A venue capturing the whole card when only one fact is needed.

title: Current-staff check for a corporate-discount purchase at a telco or retailer counter
moment: A person buys a phone plan or appliance at a store under an employee-benefit partnership, and the clerk photocopies the employee badge and ID card to confirm the buyer works at the partner company.
verifier: Telco or retail store clerk running a corporate-partner discount (企業員工專案)
predicate: Holder is a current employee of the partner company today, not a former one still carrying an old badge.
disclosed_today: Photo of the employee badge, ID card copy, sometimes a payslip, giving name, ID number, department and photo.
issuer: The partner employer, signing a freshness-bound 'currently employed here' status and revoking it when the person leaves.
why_zk: Badges and old certificates stay valid long after someone leaves, which is the abuse the store worries about, so a revocable current proof fits well. The store needs only 'is staff of company X'; the name and ID number are not needed. This echoes the telco weakness of checking only easily copied identifiers. A limit is that the proof must still show which company, so that fact is disclosed, and the store gains little incentive to change a counter routine.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A service demanding identity documents under threat of suspension without stating purpose or offering a lighter alternative.

title: Active-worker status for a gig or dispatch platform's insurance and shift eligibility
moment: A person signs up for evening shifts through a staffing or delivery platform and the platform asks them to upload an ID copy and a letter from their main employer to confirm that they are still employed elsewhere and so covered by labour insurance, avoiding duplicate enrolment.
verifier: Staffing, gig or delivery platform onboarding team (人力派遣 / 外送平台)
predicate: Person is currently enrolled and active with a primary employer today, so the platform need not enrol them separately; no employer identity or pay is revealed.
disclosed_today: ID copy with address, a letter or labour-insurance record naming the primary employer, sometimes pay records.
issuer: The primary employer, signing an 'active insured employee' status and revoking it on separation.
why_zk: The platform needs a current yes or no on active coverage, and a stale letter is useless for this. A revocable employer signature gives freshness, and hides the main employer, which the worker may not want a side-job platform to know (and some contracts restrict moonlighting). Honest weakness: the platform may be legally entitled to query labour-insurance records directly, and the worker may not want the primary employer to know a status was issued at all, since issuing could itself tip off the employer.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that collecting an ID number and salary for a simple continuing-employment check exceeds the necessary scope of purpose, with no mechanism to enforce it.
Field selection at presentation time, tightened so only the freshness predicate is released rather than whole records.

title: Still-employed proof for landlord rent-guarantee renewal
moment: A tenant renews a lease mid-term and the landlord or rental-management company asks for proof that the tenant is still employed, as a condition of keeping a reduced deposit.
verifier: Landlord or property management / rental platform
predicate: Employer has signed within the last 7 days that this holder is currently an active employee (not terminated, not on unpaid leave beyond a threshold); signature is revocable on resignation.
disclosed_today: Photocopy of the employment certificate (在職證明) or labor insurance enrollment record showing full name, ID number, employer, salary band, enrollment date; often photographed and kept in LINE chats.
issuer: Employer (HR system) issuing a short-lived employment-status credential into the wallet.
why_zk: The landlord only needs "employed as of this week", not name, ID number, or salary. Weakness: landlords often also want a name to put on the lease, so full anonymity is unrealistic; the gain is dropping salary, ID number and employer details and making a stale paper certificate useless. A static certificate can be months old, while a revocable freshness proof expires on resignation.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The concern that a stored credential gets presented repeatedly and lets an observer link the same holder across visits, so each presentation should be unlinkable.
The lack of any proof that what was released was minimal; here the proof itself is the minimal release.

title: Staff-only discount and access at a company-partnered gym or clinic
moment: An employee walks into a gym, dental clinic or cafeteria operator that has a corporate partnership with their employer and wants the staff rate; the counter must confirm the person is currently employed there, not a former employee with an old badge.
verifier: Partner gym, clinic, or vendor front desk
predicate: Employer signed within the last 24 hours that the holder is a current employee of this company (presented as a member of the partner group, without name).
disclosed_today: Staff ID card or badge photo, sometimes a name, employee number and a phone number written on a sign-up sheet; the vendor then keeps the list and may never be told when someone leaves.
issuer: Employer, signing a daily or weekly employment-status token; revoking it at departure.
why_zk: The vendor needs only "currently an employee of the partner company", and an unlinkable proof prevents the vendor from building a profile of who visits and how often. Revocation stops ex-staff from using old badges, which the vendor cannot check today. Weakness: for gyms with membership accounts the vendor already has a name and payment details, so privacy gains apply mostly to walk-in or one-off services.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The fixed-moment structure, where the claim must hold at submission and opening while identifying wrappers are handled without exposing content.
The pattern of a verifier examining identity documents with unspecified retention, which the status proof would replace.

title: Current-employee check for a sealed corporate-purchase or tender-staff conflict declaration
moment: A procurement officer at a public body or large firm needs evidence that a bidder's named evaluator or subcontract signer is currently employed by the bidding company, without receiving the employee's personnel record, before a tender opening.
verifier: Procurement or tender-opening officer
predicate: Employer signed, bound to the tender's opening date, that the holder is a current employee in a role authorised to sign; the signature is fresh as of the submission cut-off and can be revoked if the person leaves before opening.
disclosed_today: Company letter with seal (公司大小章), authorisation letter, copy of the signer's ID card and sometimes labor insurance record, enclosed with the sealed bid.
issuer: Employer (company authorised signatory) issuing a status credential.
why_zk: The officer needs only "this signer is currently authorised by this employer", yet receives a pile of personal documents that stay in a tender file for years. Freshness tied to the opening moment replaces a letter that could be stale. Weakness: Taiwan procurement rules generally require identified signers and seals, and the bid file must be auditable, so the signer cannot realistically be anonymous; the gain is limited to dropping ID copies and insurance records.

title: Pet boarding and grooming intake without exposing owner's animal-abuse record
moment: Booking a multi-day stay at a pet hotel or applying to adopt from a private shelter; the operator wants assurance the person is not on the registered list of those penalized under the Animal Protection Act (e.g., banned from keeping animals).
verifier: Pet hotel, private rescue group, or adoption platform
predicate: Holder is not on the competent authority's register of persons prohibited from keeping or adopting animals (non-membership in a sanction list).
disclosed_today: Full ID card photo, name, address, phone, sometimes a hand-written declaration; shelters may also ask for household and employment details.
issuer: Ministry of Agriculture / local animal protection office (Animal Protection Act enforcement)
why_zk: Weak-to-moderate. Today no public, queryable register exists for private operators, so the authority would first have to publish a signed absence attestation, which needs legislative backing. Private shelters collect ID mainly for contact and identification, not only for the ban check, so ZK removes only part of the over-collection. Still, an absence-only proof avoids storing ID copies in small businesses with weak data hygiene.

title: Tenant screening without handing over full ID for a stalking or protection-order check
moment: A landlord or a shared-housing (cohabitation) operator screens a prospective roommate or tenant in a female-only or family-oriented building and wants to know the applicant is not subject to an active protection order or sex-offender community notification/registration under the Sexual Assault Crime Prevention Act.
verifier: Landlord, shared-housing operator, or rental platform
predicate: Holder does not appear on the sex-offender registration/notification register nor is subject to an active protection order restricting residence near others.
disclosed_today: ID card copy, household registration transcript, criminal record certificate (which shows far more than needed), employer letter, sometimes family details.
issuer: Ministry of the Interior / National Police Agency, or Judicial Yuan for court orders
why_zk: Legally weak and sensitive: Taiwan law restricts disclosure of such registers and operators are not entitled to ask about them in general, so any use would need an explicit statutory carve-out and risks discrimination and rehabilitation harms. The honest case is that where a police clearance is already requested, an absence-only proof is far less intrusive than a full criminal record certificate, which reveals every conviction.

title: Joining a community or school volunteer role without disclosing a full police record
moment: Signing up as an after-school tutor, a temple or community-centre volunteer, or a sports coach for minors; the organisation must confirm the person is not on the list of those barred from working with children under child and youth welfare rules, but today collects the full non-criminal-record certificate.
verifier: Cram school, community association, sports club, or school volunteer coordinator
predicate: Holder is not on the register of persons barred from working with children and youths (e.g., convicted of listed offences or subject to employment bans).
disclosed_today: Police criminal record certificate (with full history of conviction categories), national ID number, home address, photo, sometimes household registration transcript.
issuer: Ministry of Health and Welfare / Ministry of Education (employment-ban registers), via Ministry of Justice records
why_zk: Strongest of the three: a legal duty to check already exists in some settings, and the record certificate over-discloses. A signed non-membership claim limited to the relevant ban list would satisfy the duty while keeping unrelated old or minor entries private. Hurdles are that the legal check is sometimes defined as a specific certificate form, so rules would need to accept the proof, and freshness (short validity or revocation) matters because bans can be imposed after issuance.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The registry answers only a narrow yes/no about its own record rather than releasing the underlying data, as the household registry does for duplicate ID numbers.
Presenting an unlinkable proof of a prior check so the agency cannot match it back to the issuance event.

title: Not on the restricted-exit list when booking a package tour
moment: A traveler pays a deposit for an overseas group tour or a visa-assisted trip, and the travel agency asks for a passport copy and ID card copy to check that the traveler is not barred from leaving the country.
verifier: Travel agency (旅行社) booking desk
predicate: Holder does not appear on the national restricted-exit (限制出境) register as of today
disclosed_today: Full photocopy of the ID card (national ID number, address, photo) and passport (passport number, birth date, photo), kept in agency files
issuer: Ministry of the Interior National Immigration Agency (內政部移民署), as the keeper of the restricted-exit register
why_zk: The agency needs only the absence from the register, not identity documents. Weakness: restricted-exit status can change after signing, so the proof needs a short validity window or a freshness timestamp. Law may also restrict who is allowed to learn restriction status at all, and the agency often needs the passport anyway for the actual ticket and visa, so the saving is only at the deposit stage. A blind or unlinkable proof also stops the agency and the issuer from correlating who is traveling.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The principle that the relying party gets what the service needs and no more, instead of the whole attestation record.
The narrower answer (no overdue case) is enough to settle the question, so the full figures need not be released.

title: Not a delinquent taxpayer when a seller registers on a marketplace or bids for a small public contract
moment: A sole proprietor or freelancer signs up to sell on an online platform or to bid for a small municipal procurement and is asked to prove they have no overdue taxes or tax-collection restrictions.
verifier: Online marketplace onboarding team or a city-government procurement clerk
predicate: Holder is not on the list of persons with overdue taxes or with enforced-collection or restricted-exit tax cases (欠稅 / 移送執行名單) at issuance time
disclosed_today: A full tax-clearance certificate (完稅證明 / 無欠稅證明) showing taxpayer name, ID number, and often tax amounts or income categories, plus a business registration copy
issuer: Ministry of Finance National Taxation Bureau (財政部國稅局), or the local tax bureau for local taxes
why_zk: Today the clearance paper carries tax detail the verifier does not need; a signed non-membership claim reveals only that no overdue case exists. Weakness: tax authority records are confidential by law (稅捐稽徵法 secrecy), so the bureau may refuse to sign anything but the existing certificate, and procurement rules may name the paper certificate explicitly. Also, absence from a list is only as good as the list's update frequency, so the proof must carry an as-of date.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A single yes/no fact delivered so that neither the verifier nor the issuer can track the holder.
The warning that a request category can bundle extra fields (issuer, photo), which here mirrors the good-conduct certificate bundling unrelated record details.

title: Not a sex-offender-registry entry when joining a cram school or sports club as a part-time coach
moment: A university student or retiree applies as an after-school tutor, swim coach, or children's activity assistant, and the employer asks for a police criminal-record certificate and a check against child-protection restriction lists before the first class.
verifier: Cram school (補習班), sports club, or after-school care operator
predicate: Holder does not appear on the sexual-offense or child-protection employment-restriction register (性侵害加害人 / 兒少性剝削 登記查閱名單) at issuance time
disclosed_today: A police good-conduct certificate (良民證) or a similar paper listing full name, ID number, birth date and a statement about the full criminal-record status, which can expose unrelated, old, or expunged entries
issuer: Ministry of the Interior Police Administration (內政部警政署) or the competent local education or social-welfare bureau
why_zk: The employer's legitimate need is only absence from the restriction register; a good-conduct certificate shows more than that, including minor records unrelated to children. Weakness: Taiwanese child-protection law already obliges employers to query specific lists through official channels, and the legally required check may have to be performed by the employer directly with the authority rather than accepting a holder's proof, so a wallet proof may be legally insufficient unless regulations are updated. Freshness is also critical here, because a register entry added after the proof was signed would be missed.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A check that relies only on copyable ID details is weak, which motivates a signed, fresh, holder-bound proof of the register status instead of a passport photocopy.
The idea that leakage should be bounded and checkable, applied by making the only thing the verifier learns a single yes bit about the register.

title: Proving no outstanding exit restriction at the airport check-in counter
moment: A Taiwanese traveler checks in for an international flight, and the airline or ground handler must confirm the passenger is not subject to a government travel ban (出境限制, for example from tax arrears or court orders) before issuing a boarding pass, or a travel agent confirms it before booking a non-refundable group tour.
verifier: Airline ground-handling staff or a travel agency booking desk
predicate: The holder's national ID is not on the current exit-restriction register (non-membership), signed with a short validity window.
disclosed_today: Full passport and national ID number, often copied or photographed. If a restriction exists, staff can see it, and the traveler may be questioned about the reason in front of others.
issuer: National Immigration Agency, drawing on court and tax-authority restriction records
why_zk: A non-membership proof would let the verifier see only that the person is not restricted, so a clear traveler reveals nothing else. Weakness, stated honestly. Border control (immigration at departure) already checks the register itself and carriers have little legal duty to check, so this mostly removes a copy of the passport rather than a real check. A restricted person simply cannot produce the proof, and that failure itself tells the verifier something. The proof must be fresh, because a restriction can be imposed hours before departure.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A record that identifies a person should not become a readable file kept by the collector; the verifier here keeps only a yes bit and not a copied certificate.
The open-ended exception that lets collectors keep data they say they need, which is the reason a proof that never hands over the data is stronger than a promise to delete it.

title: Showing a nanny or tutor is not on the sex-offender notification register
moment: A parent hires a private after-school tutor, a babysitter from a platform, or a cram-school teaches a trial class, and the hiring side wants assurance the person is not on the sexual-offender registry (性侵害加害人登記). Today they ask for a police record certificate (良民證) from the candidate.
verifier: A parent, a childcare or tutoring platform, or a small cram-school owner
predicate: The holder is not on the sexual-offence offender registration or notification list (non-membership), plus the signing authority and date.
disclosed_today: A full criminal-record certificate, which can reveal unrelated old convictions, offences already expunged in practice, and the candidate's complete identity details, and is photocopied and kept by the employer.
issuer: Ministry of the Interior (police administration), or the Ministry of Justice for the criminal record side
why_zk: A narrow non-membership claim says only that the person is not on this specific register, instead of handing over a whole record that lets an employer judge unrelated matters. Weakness, stated honestly. For jobs covered by child-protection law, the employer is legally required to check specific registries and may be entitled to the fuller record, so the narrow proof would not replace the legal check, and informal parents may actually want more than a register absence. The proof also covers only the registry, not every risk, so it can give false comfort.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A record of where and when a person went can become a readable log of their life, so the verifier should not be given the underlying list.
Splitting knowledge so no single party holds both identity and detail, applied by letting the verifier know the person is clear without learning the identity-linked violation history.

title: Proving a vehicle owner has no unpaid traffic fines before a used-car sale transfer
moment: A buyer at a second-hand car dealer, or a private seller, needs the seller to show that the seller has no unpaid traffic fines or license-suspension notices attached to them or the plate before ownership transfer is processed at the motor vehicle office or agreed privately.
verifier: A used-car dealer or a private buyer, and sometimes an escrow or insurance agent
predicate: The holder is not on the list of persons with outstanding unpaid traffic penalties or an active licence suspension (non-membership), tied to the holder, not to a photo of a document.
disclosed_today: Full ID card, driver licence photo, vehicle licence and registration details, and sometimes screenshots of the government fine-lookup page showing the entire list of violations with dates and places.
issuer: Directorate General of Highways (Ministry of Transportation and Communications) or the Motor Vehicles Office
why_zk: A dealer needs only that nothing is outstanding, yet the usual screenshot reveals where and when the seller drove, which hints at routines and locations. A non-membership proof removes that history. Weakness, stated honestly. Outstanding fines are already tied to the plate and the transfer office blocks the transfer itself, so the private-sale buyer gains limited protection, the benefit is mainly privacy of the seller, and the incentive for a dealer to ask for anything less than the full look-up is low. A fine imposed minutes later invalidates the proof, so it needs a short expiry.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The pattern of a private counterparty collecting full front-and-back ID copies when only one narrow fact is needed.
The household register transcript as an over-broad document that is shown or handed over for a narrow purpose.

title: Proving no outstanding exit restriction when buying a used car at a dealer
moment: A buyer or seller at a used-car dealership or consignment lot in Taiwan needs the vehicle transfer to go through, and the dealer wants assurance the seller is not under a travel or asset restriction and the car is not seized. Today the dealer photocopies the seller's ID, license and often household register.
verifier: Used-car dealer or consignment broker
predicate: The seller's national ID is NOT on the court or administrative enforcement (seizure / transfer-restriction) register for this vehicle's plate at the time of signing.
disclosed_today: Front-and-back ID copy, driver's license copy, sometimes household register transcript with address and family members; the dealer keeps the copies in the deal folder.
issuer: Directorate General of Highways / MVDO jointly with Judicial Yuan enforcement records (government signs a non-membership attestation over the restriction register).
why_zk: The dealer only needs absence from a seizure/restriction list, not who the seller is beyond the transacting identity. Weakness: the dealer still needs a legal name for the contract and the transfer form, so identity cannot be fully hidden; the real gain is dropping the extra copies and household data. Also depends on an agency actually publishing a signed, timestamped absence attestation, which does not exist today.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A verifier carrying out an identity and risk check with document inspection where retention and scope are unspecified.

title: Showing a landlord that a tenant is not on the public-housing or rent-subsidy disqualification list
moment: A tenant applying to a private landlord that participates in the government social-housing sublease scheme, or a landlord renting under a subsidy program, must show the applicant is not disqualified for owning other property or prior fraud. The agency or landlord's agent collects tax and property records.
verifier: Landlord or intermediary operator under the sublease-subsidy program
predicate: The applicant is NOT on the register of persons disqualified or blacklisted from housing subsidy for prior false declaration or recovered overpayment.
disclosed_today: Full property ownership transcript, income tax records, household composition, and ID copies delivered to the operator.
issuer: Ministry of the Interior Construction and Planning Agency (or local housing bureau) as keeper of the disqualification list.
why_zk: The operator needs only that the person is not blacklisted, but the program itself legally also requires income and property eligibility checks, which are positive predicates and not covered by non-membership; so this removes only the blacklist part of the file. Weakness: the blacklist is small and the operator may be entitled to query it directly, in which case ZK adds little over a direct government lookup.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea of separating an eligibility check from the record that is kept, so the verifier learns eligibility without the underlying file.

title: Proving not being on the court-ordered debtor restriction list when taking a school-bus or after-school care contract
moment: A parent enrolling a child with a private after-school care or school-bus operator is asked for a guarantor or prepayment, and the operator wants assurance the parent is not under a court-ordered restriction (such as a debtor under compulsory enforcement or restricted from leaving the country). It is applied as a general screen by some operators.
verifier: Private after-school care or school-bus operator
predicate: The parent is NOT on the compulsory-enforcement debtor register maintained by the courts.
disclosed_today: Parent's ID copy, contact details, sometimes bank account statement or proof of employment to show solvency.
issuer: Judicial Yuan / district court enforcement office.
why_zk: A signed absence from the debtor register would replace bank statements and employment proof with a single bit. Weakness: this is a weak and legally questionable use, since screening parents on debtor status for child care may be discriminatory or unlawful under consumer and children's-services rules, and the real proof of future payment capacity is not captured by non-membership. It is included to show where the pattern is thin rather than a recommended deployment.

title: Dormitory/communal-housing "no contagious infection" clearance during an outbreak window
moment: A university dorm, long-term-care facility, or migrant-worker dormitory re-opens after a legionella, tuberculosis, or enterovirus alert and asks incoming residents or returning staff to show they are cleared to share rooms.
verifier: Dormitory administrator or facility infection-control officer
predicate: Hospital has cleared the person of the named communicable condition (screening negative or isolation completed) and the clearance is valid from issue date until the end of the outbreak watch period (e.g. 14 or 30 days).
disclosed_today: A photocopy of the hospital certificate or lab report (diagnosis, test results, physician notes), or a health-declaration form with symptom history; sometimes a full medical certificate stored in a paper folder.
issuer: Hospital (infection-control or outpatient department)
why_zk: The facility only needs "cleared during this window" and not the disease history, test values or other conditions on the report. Honest caveat is that infectious-disease handling is regulated by the Communicable Disease Control Act, so a facility may be legally entitled to ask for more in an active case, and a hospital would have to agree to issue wallet credentials at all. Weak where public health authorities mandate direct reporting rather than self-presented proof.

title: Employer sick-leave or surgery-recovery verification for a specific absence period
moment: An employee is hospitalised or has outpatient surgery and the HR department wants proof that the absence is genuine and covers a date range, before approving paid sick leave or the Labor Standards Act sick-leave allowance.
verifier: Employer HR or payroll department
predicate: A hospital-signed attestation that the holder was medically unfit for work for the dates from X to Y (credential valid only for that interval), with no diagnosis.
disclosed_today: Diagnosis certificate (診斷證明書) listing the diagnosis, procedure, ward, treating physician and recommended rest days; HR staff and sometimes line managers see the whole certificate.
issuer: Hospital (attending physician or medical records office)
why_zk: HR needs only "unfit for work 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09"; the diagnosis (cancer, mental health, pregnancy complications) is sensitive and employers do not need it. Honest caveat is that some employers and insurers contractually demand the diagnosis certificate, and employees may not feel free to refuse; also the attestation of a date range is easy to build with a signed range credential, so ZK adds little beyond selective disclosure of two fields. The privacy gain is real, but the adoption barrier is employer practice and not cryptography.

title: Visitor access to a school or kindergarten after a child's infection with a fixed exclusion period
moment: A child returns to kindergarten or primary school after hand-foot-mouth disease, influenza or COVID, and the school requires proof the child is no longer contagious and has served the exclusion period, which is time-bounded by health-department guidance.
verifier: School nurse or kindergarten administrator
predicate: A hospital-signed status "cleared to return" valid from the clearance date for the rest of the school term or a stated number of days, without disclosing which illness or the treatment.
disclosed_today: Hospital medical certificate or the parent's handwritten statement plus the doctor's note naming the disease, symptoms and medication; some schools photograph the note into class records.
issuer: Hospital (paediatrics department)
why_zk: The school only needs "may attend, no isolation required" for the relevant window, not the child's diagnosis or medication, which can reveal chronic conditions. Honest caveat is that schools in Taiwan are required to report certain notifiable diseases and nurses may legitimately need the disease name to manage class-level outbreaks, so a pure no-detail proof can conflict with public health practice. The minor's data also raises guardian-consent and issuer-liability questions.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that release should be limited to what the stated purpose needs, here made checkable by a proof instead of left to the holder's judgment.
The pattern of proving one yes/no fact without revealing the underlying record and without letting the issuer track where it is used.

title: Sick-leave validity window for a school or exam make-up without the diagnosis
moment: A parent in Taiwan asks a school to excuse a child's absence from a midterm or a school trip, or a university student asks for a make-up exam after illness. The school asks for the diagnosis certificate (診斷證明書) to be photocopied or photographed and sent over LINE or the school portal.
verifier: School administrative office or university registrar
predicate: A hospital physician attests that the holder was medically unfit to attend school or sit exams between date A and date B. The proof is valid only for that window and reveals no diagnosis, department or treatment.
disclosed_today: Full diagnosis certificate showing the diagnosis, the ICD wording, the physician, the department, the full name and the national ID number. It is often kept in the student file or sent through a class group chat.
issuer: Treating hospital, via its physician-signed certificate system
why_zk: A school needs only that the absence was medically justified on specific days. A time-bounded, selectively disclosed attestation does this, and it also removes the temptation to forge or edit a scanned certificate. It is weaker where school regulations explicitly ask for the diagnosis, for example for infectious diseases that trigger class suspension rules. In those cases the diagnosis may be legally required, so the proof would need a separate disclosed field.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Presenting an unlinkable proof of a prior check so the verifier cannot match the redemption to the original hospital visit or to the holder's other visits.
The idea that a shared record should have the identifying and unrelated fields stripped so the leftover cannot re-identify the person.

title: Proof of recent negative infectious-disease clearance for a short-stay care-facility or day-care visit
moment: A visitor, volunteer or new aide at a nursing home, long-term care center or kindergarten has to show they were tested or cleared (for example no active TB, influenza or norovirus symptoms) within the past few days before entering. Staff today often ask for a photo of the lab report or hospital slip at the door.
verifier: Long-term care facility, nursing home or kindergarten staff at the entrance or HR desk
predicate: A hospital signs a status of cleared for entry, valid only for N days from the test date. The verifier checks that the status is still in its window and learns neither the test type, the result detail nor any other clinical content.
disclosed_today: The entire lab or screening report, with the name, ID number, test types, other tested items and often the hospital visit details.
issuer: Hospital laboratory or infection-control department
why_zk: The facility cares about whether the holder is cleared right now, not about what else was tested. The signed validity window encodes freshness without a live lookup, so the facility does not need access to hospital systems. The weakness is that facilities often want a paper record for inspection audits, and local health authorities may specify which documents to retain, so a pure proof may not satisfy an auditor.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The notion of content that stays unseen by intermediate handlers until a fixed moment, with the wrapper readable only for what is needed to identify it.
The purpose-limited release principle, where only the part that serves the travel decision is exposed.

title: Hospital-signed fit-to-fly or fit-to-travel window for an airline or ferry to the outlying islands
moment: A passenger recovering from surgery, late pregnancy or a heart event books a flight to Kinmen, Penghu or Lanyu, or a long-haul flight, and the carrier or tour operator asks for a doctor's fitness note. Staff photocopy or photograph the note and sometimes keep it with the booking.
verifier: Airline check-in counter, ferry operator or travel agent handling the booking
predicate: A hospital physician signs that the holder is medically fit to travel for a trip on dates within a stated window, and the proof stops being valid after the window. No diagnosis, procedure, gestational detail or medication is shown.
disclosed_today: A medical certificate with the diagnosis, the procedure or gestational age, the medications, the physician details and the full ID number. It is copied and stored with the booking records.
issuer: Treating hospital (attending physician's office)
why_zk: The carrier's decision is only whether it may carry the passenger on that date. A time-bound signature matches the fact that fitness for travel can change within days. The sealed-bid analogy applies to the content, which stays hidden from handlers until the moment of use. This is weak where the airline's own medical-clearance form (MEDIF) requires specific clinical fields that the airline's medical desk reviews, in which case the proof would only cover the simpler cases, such as ferries and domestic routes.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Release only the single attribute the transaction needs rather than the whole credential.
Checking only easily copied identifiers (a paper copy) lets someone else pass, so the proof should be bound to the holder and signed by the issuer.

title: Hospital-signed 'infection-free window' for a hospital-ward caregiver or private nursing-home visitor
moment: A family member or foreign live-in caregiver (外籍看護) arrives at a Taiwanese nursing home or a ward during an outbreak and must show they recently tested negative or are not in an infectious period.
verifier: Nursing home (護理之家) front desk or ward access control
predicate: Hospital attests 'no active infectious-disease restriction' valid from test date to test date + N days (e.g. 7 days); nothing else.
disclosed_today: Photo or paper of the lab report or clinic certificate showing diagnosis, test type, lab values, name, ID number, and sometimes medication.
issuer: Hospital or clinic laboratory that ran the test
why_zk: The verifier only needs a yes for the window, but today the whole report is shown or photographed and kept on a staff phone. Validity expiry is built into the claim, so no clinical detail is needed. Weakness: nursing homes mostly act on paper habits and no regulation requires accepting a digital proof, and a window set by each facility's own policy may not match what the hospital signed.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Wallet releases only the needed attribute from a credential issued as a whole.
Confidentiality being only a discretionary exception, with full disclosure as the default, is the pattern to flip so minimal disclosure is the default.

title: Postpartum or post-surgery 'not fit to travel / fit to return' window for employer leave and insurer claims
moment: An employee on 病假 or 產假 extension submits a doctor's certificate to HR, or a patient submits it to a travel insurer, to show they were medically unable to work or travel on specific dates.
verifier: Employer HR department or travel/health insurer claims desk
predicate: Hospital attests 'medically unfit for work/travel for the period [start, end]' as a boolean over a date range, with no diagnosis.
disclosed_today: 診斷證明書 with diagnosis name, ICD code, procedures, and attending physician notes, sent to HR or insurer by scan or email.
issuer: Treating hospital
why_zk: HR needs only that the absence is covered for those dates, yet diagnosis certificates reveal pregnancy complications, psychiatric conditions, or surgery type to a manager. A time-bounded proof removes the diagnosis. Weakness: Taiwanese labour rules and insurers often legally require the diagnosis or the original certificate, and insurers may need the cause to adjudicate, so adoption depends on rule changes rather than on technology.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Express the leak as a bounded, checkable quantity: here the verifier learns only a category and expiry, and nothing else can be inferred.
A stable identifier that outlives its context keeps working for others, so the proof must expire and not be tied to a permanent number.

title: Hospital-signed 'currently in treatment course' status for a pharmacy or school to grant a temporary accommodation
moment: A parent asks a school for a short-term accommodation (exempting a child from PE or the cafeteria, or allowing a medication break) or a worker asks a company for a temporary shift change during a defined treatment cycle such as chemotherapy or post-fracture recovery.
verifier: School health office (健康中心), employer, or gym/pool operator
predicate: Hospital attests 'accommodation category X applies' valid until the course end date, auto-expiring afterward.
disclosed_today: Hospital certificate or discharge summary naming the disease and treatment plan, often photocopied and kept in the school file indefinitely.
issuer: Treating hospital
why_zk: The school needs a category and an end date, not that a child has cancer or a worker has a particular condition. Expiry removes the problem of a stale record being kept after recovery and then used for other purposes. Weakness: a coded accommodation category needs to be agreed between hospitals and schools, and teachers often want a conversation with the family, so the proof may not replace it.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A single yes/no claim proved without revealing the underlying record, with no tracking by issuer or verifier.
The idea that a host should check a document and not keep a copy of it, applied to travellers' health papers.

title: Fit-to-fly / low-infection-risk window for a cruise or group-tour boarding
moment: A traveller boards a cruise ship at Keelung or joins a group tour, and the operator asks for a recent negative test, a vaccination record or a doctor's note showing no infectious illness in the last few days.
verifier: Cruise line or tour operator boarding desk
predicate: Hospital attests "cleared of notifiable infectious condition" and the attestation is valid only for the 72 hours around departure (valid-from / valid-to window), nothing else.
disclosed_today: Full lab report or clinic certificate with name, ID number, diagnosis context, test type, clinic and physician, kept as a photocopy or photo by the operator.
issuer: Hospital or its outpatient clinic, signing a short-lived status credential into the digital wallet.
why_zk: The operator only needs a yes/no that is true on departure day, and the proof should expire by itself instead of becoming a stored medical file. Weak points to be honest about: operators may be required by quarantine or port rules to keep records, and a hospital would need to issue such a status in real time, which is not standard practice.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A gatekeeper only needs to know that a prior check was passed, without receiving a persistent identifier.

title: Post-surgery or post-procedure "may be left alone / cleared for pickup" window for a ride or care service
moment: After day surgery or a colonoscopy under sedation, the patient is collected by a family member, a taxi or a nursing-aide service that asks for the discharge summary to prove the patient is cleared to leave and who is responsible.
verifier: Taxi or care-transport dispatcher, home-care agency, or a hotel or recovery guesthouse near the hospital
predicate: Hospital signs "discharged in stable condition, may travel or stay unaccompanied after time T" and it is valid only for the next 24 hours.
disclosed_today: The whole discharge note, including diagnosis, procedure name, medications and attending doctor, photographed or handed over on paper.
issuer: Hospital discharge system issuing a time-limited status.
why_zk: The service needs only the clearance and the time window, not the procedure, and a short validity stops the status being reused later. Honest limits: many such services rely on a person's word and have no wallet reader, so adoption incentive is low, and some care agencies legitimately need medication information for safety.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A record-keeping duty that relies on each institution's good policy rather than technical limits, which a timed proof would replace with a technical limit.
The problem that a check ends up capturing the whole document and needs a cap on what is retained.

title: Contagion-free window for a school or childcare return after an illness
moment: A child returns to kindergarten or an after-school care centre (afterschool "anqinban") after hand-foot-mouth disease, influenza or another notifiable illness, and staff ask for the doctor's certificate to confirm the child is no longer contagious.
verifier: Kindergarten, childcare centre or after-school class
predicate: Hospital signs "not contagious from date A", valid for the school term week in which the child returns, and optionally "not contagious through date B" for rolling attendance.
disclosed_today: The clinic certificate or medical receipt showing the diagnosis, sometimes the whole medical visit record, which is often photographed by staff and kept in a messaging group.
issuer: Hospital or paediatric clinic.
why_zk: The centre only needs to know the child may attend within a bounded period, not the diagnosis. Other parents' messaging groups and staff phones are where such records leak today. Honest limits: centres often have a legal duty to report notifiable diseases to health authorities, so some disclosure is legitimate and the proof can only replace the over-collection, not the reporting; parents of young children may have no wallet in place of the child.

title: Delivery-platform courier rating for a building management committee hire
moment: A residential community (社區) in Taipei hires a part-time package-room or night-shift concierge, or lets a gig courier get a building access tag. The management committee wants evidence of reliability.
verifier: Community management committee (管理委員會) or its property management company
predicate: Lifetime completed deliveries on a delivery platform is at least 500 AND average customer rating is at least 4.7
disclosed_today: Screenshots of the courier app profile showing real name, photo, phone number, order history, earnings, and city zones worked
issuer: Delivery platform account (Uber Eats / foodpanda courier app), attested via zkTLS over the logged-in session; the platform never agreed to issue credentials
why_zk: Screenshots leak earnings and movement patterns, and are trivially faked or edited. A zkTLS threshold proof shows only that the count and rating clear the bar. Weakness: platform terms of service may forbid scraping or proving from the session, ratings are platform-internal and gameable, and the committee may legally prefer a police record certificate for access-sensitive roles.

title: Ride-hailing driver tenure for a fleet-lease or insurance quote
moment: A Taiwan Taxi (台灣大車隊) or Uber driver applies for a lower-premium commercial auto policy or a leased vehicle from a fleet owner, who wants proof of steady driving history.
verifier: Fleet leasing company or commercial auto insurer's agent
predicate: Active trips completed in the last 12 months is at least 3000 AND account age is at least 24 months
