verifier: University or research-institute human resources and payroll office
predicate: The holder of a university-signed enrolment and supervisor-approval credential is the same person as the holder of a government-issued work-eligibility credential (work permit or labour insurance status), proven without revealing passport or ARC number to the department that only needs to approve the hire.
disclosed_today: Passport and ARC copy, enrolment certificate, work-permit scan, bank details, handed to department staff who are not payroll specialists and often keep photocopies in unsecured folders.
issuer: University (enrolment and approval claim), matched to the Ministry of Labor or immigration agency (work eligibility claim)
why_zk: Department-level staff pass around scans of passports and ARCs that only payroll and compliance truly need, creating a leakage risk for foreigners in particular. A matched proof lets the department confirm eligibility while the identifier goes only to payroll. The weakness is that the university is itself the verifier and an employer, with a legal duty to retain a copy of the work permit and ARC for labour inspection, so zero-knowledge can reduce who sees the data inside the institution but cannot remove the retention requirement.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The university signs the enrollment claim without needing to see the second issuer's identifier, which the holder binds only at presentation.
A single yes/no fact is proven with no trackable identifier passed to the verifier or issuer.

title: Student-status discount tied to the same person as the transit or telecom account
moment: A student buys a youth/student monthly pass or a campus-plan mobile subscription, and the seller must be sure the enrolled student is the same person as the account holder.
verifier: Transit operator student-pass counter or telecom reseller
predicate: The university-signed "currently enrolled" claim and the national-ID-bound claim in the wallet refer to the same person, without revealing the ID number or student number.
disclosed_today: Student ID card photo, national ID card photo or number, birth date, school name, student number, sometimes a photocopy kept on file.
issuer: University (enrollment status), matched against a second issuer such as the MOI digital ID or a telecom account
why_zk: A cross-source match proves one person holds both claims, and the verifier needs nothing else. Weakness is that a student card is a physical norm and clerks may still insist on seeing it, and the Personal Data Protection Act already limits copying but does not forbid it in practice. Telecom real-name rules require the ID be recorded, so the telecom case is weaker than the transit pass.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The registry-style answer is narrowed to the one fact needed (same person or not) instead of releasing the identifier itself.
The proof attests to a prior check without letting the verifier link it to the issuance or to other uses.

title: Dorm or campus-housing landlord checks tenant is the enrolled student named on the lease deposit subsidy
moment: A private landlord renting near a university takes a student tenant who claims a rent subsidy or student-rate lease, and the landlord's bank or local-government subsidy office needs to confirm the tenant is the enrolled student.
verifier: Private landlord or housing subsidy office
predicate: The university enrollment claim and the tenant's government-issued identity claim belong to the same person, with the ID number and student number withheld.
disclosed_today: Full ID card copy, student ID copy, home address, parents' contact details, sometimes a transcript or enrollment certificate.
issuer: University (enrollment), matched against the national digital ID or household registration credential
why_zk: Landlords routinely keep ID photocopies that leak in later disputes; a same-person proof gives them enough to rely on the student status. However, lease practice in Taiwan often wants a real address and a guarantor, and subsidy offices may legally require the full ID number, so the proof only replaces the enrollment-copy part, not the whole file.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A verifier accepts proof of an earlier check without being able to link it to the issuing event.
A discretionary fuller-disclosure exception, here for occupational health, remains alongside the minimal proof.

title: Hospital internship or clinical-placement badge matched to professional licence
moment: A nursing or medical student starts a clinical placement at a teaching hospital, and the hospital must confirm the university-enrolled student is the same person as the holder of a separate vaccination or background-check record from another issuer.
verifier: Hospital HR or placement coordinator
predicate: The university-signed placement-eligibility claim and the health-authority vaccination claim refer to the same person, with neither the ID number nor other health records revealed.
disclosed_today: Full vaccination card, national ID copy, student ID, sometimes a full health check report, collected into a paper file.
issuer: University (placement eligibility), matched against a second issuer such as the health authority vaccination record
why_zk: The hospital only needs to know the same person is both enrolled and vaccinated, not the full record. Honest weakness is that hospitals have occupational-health duties and may legitimately want specific vaccine details, so the match proof covers only the eligibility gate and a fuller disclosure may still be required afterwards.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that checking eligibility at the moment of sale should not require keeping a copy of the identity document.
The pattern of a point-of-sale rule that demands capturing and retaining a person's image with no less-intrusive alternative.

title: Student-rate transit pass bound to the same person as the telecom/bank account
moment: A student buys a discounted monthly commuter pass or youth fare product through a transit operator's app, which must be sure the student-status claim belongs to the same person who holds the stored-value or payment account the pass is loaded onto.
verifier: Transit operator or e-ticketing issuer (e.g. a city MRT or bus card scheme, or an e-ticket platform).
predicate: The university-signed enrolled-this-semester claim and the payment or ticketing account's holder claim refer to the same person, shown without revealing the national ID number to the operator.
disclosed_today: Photo of student ID card, sometimes national ID number and date of birth, entered or photographed at a counter or in the app, and often retained for the pass record.
issuer: University registrar (enrolment status), matched against the wallet-held account or identity credential from a second issuer.
why_zk: A same-person proof removes the need to copy the ID or student card, and the operator only learns that an enrolled student owns this account. Moderate strength: many operators already accept a simple student-card photo, and a university credential only adds value if the operator's app can verify wallet proofs and universities issue them per semester.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The problem of an office collecting identity document copies at its own discretion with no stated scope.
The weakness of a deletion duty that has an open-ended exception for what the holder says it still needs.

title: Dormitory and campus-housing off-campus lease renewal tied to a landlord-side identity record
moment: A student renting a room near campus is asked by the landlord or a rental agency to prove both that they are enrolled and that the person named on the lease is the same one the university enrolled, so the landlord can claim rent subsidy or insurance cover.
verifier: Private landlord or rental agency, and possibly a subsidy administrator reviewing the lease.
predicate: The university's signed enrolment claim and the lease or household-record claim from a second issuer (such as the household registration office) refer to the same person, without disclosing the ID number to the landlord.
disclosed_today: Photocopy of national ID card front and back, student ID, and sometimes household register transcript, kept by the agent with no stated retention limit.
issuer: University registrar, matched against a household registration or ID credential from a government issuer.
why_zk: Landlords and agents routinely collect full ID copies that stay in desk drawers and phone photos, and a match proof would let them confirm student status and identity without holding the number. Weak in practice because small landlords rarely run verifier software and the legal retention limits on private individuals are loosely enforced, so adoption would depend on a rental platform or subsidy portal requiring it.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The goal of keeping a record of who used what without it becoming a readable log of a person's interests.
The framing of seating someone for a task without the wider public learning who they are, with confidentiality being a technical default rather than a discretionary exception.

title: Library or lab-resource borrowing across two institutions
moment: A graduate student from one university wants to borrow materials or book lab equipment at a different institution's library or shared research facility under a reciprocal-access agreement, and the host must confirm the borrower is a current member of the home university and the same person who holds the host's own visitor registration.
verifier: Host institution's library desk or shared-instrument facility.
predicate: The home university's signed membership claim and the host's visitor account (issued by the host) belong to the same person, with no identifier shown to the host and no record of what the person borrowed linked to a national ID.
disclosed_today: Student card, national ID number or passport number for registering a visitor account, and a lending record tied to that identity.
issuer: Home university (membership or enrolment), matched against the host institution's own visitor credential.
why_zk: The host needs to know that a member of a partner university is the one borrowing, not who the person is across all their activity, and a match proof keeps the lending log from becoming a readable record of a person's reading interests. Reasonably strong because libraries already treat borrowing records as sensitive, but the host's visitor account is its own issuer so both credentials are in practice institution-controlled, which limits the independence of the two sources.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a counter should record only the fields a rule requires rather than keeping a full copy of the identity document.
The proof should show a prior check passed without acting as a persistent identifier across repeated purchases.

title: Alumni-discount student-ID match at a Taiwan High Speed Rail or TRA concession counter
moment: A graduate student buys a student concession fare or a campus-partner ticket at a station counter or kiosk and is asked to show a student card plus national ID so the clerk can see both names match.
verifier: Railway or bus operator concession desk, or a third-party ticketing vendor handling campus partner deals
predicate: The enrolled-student claim signed by the university and the holder of the digital wallet national-ID credential refer to the same person, shown as a match proof without revealing the national ID number or student number.
disclosed_today: Student card (name, student number, photo, department, validity sticker) and often national ID card shown side by side or photographed for the sales record.
issuer: University (enrolment status) cross-matched with the national digital wallet identity credential.
why_zk: The verifier only needs "this current student is the person standing here", yet today it sees student number, department, ID number and birthdate. A match proof between the university claim and the wallet credential avoids that. Honest weakness is that concession fares are low value and clerks are used to a quick glance at the card, so adoption pressure is small, and the in-person photo check is arguably still needed.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The list-of-identifiers-removed approach, applied by keeping the linking identifier out of the verifier's hands while still allowing a join.
The problem that a holder exposes the whole card at the moment of checking, so a field-limit rule alone does not stop over-collection.

title: Linking a university research-participant record to a hospital clinical-trial enrolment
moment: A university hospital-affiliated lab recruits a graduate student or staff member for a paid study that requires both a university-signed role claim (for example, enrolled in a health-science program) and a separate hospital or health-agency issued eligibility claim, and the study office wants to be sure both refer to the same person.
verifier: University institutional review board office or the clinical-trial coordinator
predicate: The university-signed claim and the claim from the second issuer (hospital or health insurance) belong to the same holder, shown without revealing the national ID number or health insurance number to the study office.
disclosed_today: Full name, national ID number, student number, health insurance card details and sometimes a scanned copy of both documents, stored in the study consent file.
issuer: University (program enrolment) cross-matched with a hospital or health insurance issuer.
why_zk: Study files that hold ID numbers beside health information create a re-identification risk the IRB would rather avoid, in the spirit of de-identification checklists. A cross-source match lets the coordinator confirm eligibility from two unrelated issuers without ever holding the identifier that joins them. Honest weakness is that consent forms legally require a signature and often a real name, so the study can rarely drop identification entirely; this only removes the ID number and insurance number.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The failure case where a check on copyable identifiers (ID number and issue date) let stolen data pass, motivating a holder-bound match.
Using a proof that attests an earlier check passed without handing the gatekeeper a reusable identifier.

title: Telecom student-plan SIM activation tied to a university enrolment
moment: A student applies online or in a shop for a discounted student mobile plan or a campus-partner SIM and the telecom must confirm that the enrolled student is the same named person applying, not someone using stolen identity data.
verifier: Telecom operator online applications platform or retail shop
predicate: The university-signed enrolment claim and the wallet identity credential refer to the same holder, proved with a possession-bound match instead of typing in ID number and issue date.
disclosed_today: National ID number, ID issue date, name, birthdate, student number, and sometimes uploaded photos of the ID and student card.
issuer: University (enrolment) cross-matched with the national digital wallet identity credential.
why_zk: Past fraud in Taiwan showed that checking only a national ID number and issue date lets stolen identity data pass. A holder-bound match proof replaces copyable identifiers with something that cannot be replayed by someone who merely knows the numbers, and the telecom no longer stores a student number it does not need. Honest weakness is that telecom SIM registration law still requires the operator to collect and retain the real-name ID data, so the proof would reduce but not remove the data kept; it mostly helps the student discount step.

title: Electricity-bill subsidy roll as proof of eligibility for a school lunch or after-school care fee waiver
moment: A parent enrolls a child in a public after-school care program (or applies for a lunch-fee reduction) at the start of the semester and must show proof of being a low-income or subsidised household.
verifier: School administration office / district after-school care operator
predicate: The household's utility account is a member of the set of accounts on the low-income or subsidised-rate roll (for example, accounts receiving the low-income household electricity discount).
disclosed_today: A photocopy of the full utility bill (name, address, meter number, usage in kWh, amount due) or a household certificate from the district office, plus household registration details.
issuer: Taipower (or the local water company), signing membership in the subsidised-account roll
why_zk: The school only needs a yes/no on eligibility, yet today it keeps a bill showing address and consumption patterns (which reveal when the family is away or how many people live there). Weakness is real. In practice schools usually rely on the district office's low-income household certificate (issued under the Public Assistance Act), not utility rolls, so a utility roll would only be a convenient substitute where the discount list is a recognised proxy. It also needs the school to accept it, and Taipower's discount rolls are not formally a social-welfare eligibility register.

title: Proving a tenant's subsidised-utility status to a landlord or social-housing agency without revealing the rented address
moment: A person applying for a rent subsidy or a social-housing waitlist slot must show they currently hold a utility account on the subsidised roll, but the agency is also a different locality from the one they rent in, and the applicant does not want a prospective landlord or agency to see the address and usage history.
verifier: Municipal housing bureau or social-housing intermediary (e.g. a city social housing agency or a rent-subsidy application window)
predicate: The applicant's utility account belongs to the set of accounts on the subsidised-rate roll (and is active), without revealing which account or address.
disclosed_today: Recent utility bills with address and consumption, lease copy, household registration, and sometimes several months of statements to show continuity.
issuer: Taipower / Taiwan Water Corporation
why_zk: The agency wants to know the person is a bona fide low-income occupant, but collects address, usage and the lease, which also lets staff and intermediaries profile occupancy. Honest caveat: rent-subsidy eligibility is defined by income and asset tests via the tax and household registration data, so a utility subsidy roll is only a weak, partial signal and cannot replace those checks. It is most plausible as an extra anti-fraud tie-in (the address is a real, occupied dwelling), where some fields are legitimately required by the agency anyway.

title: Medical-electricity-equipment household flag for priority outage notification or emergency-shelter registration
moment: A household that uses life-support equipment at home (ventilator, oxygen concentrator, dialysis) signs up with the city fire department or a typhoon-season emergency program to get priority power-restoration and evacuation help, and an outage-relief volunteer group or shelter operator wants to confirm the household is on the utility's medical-need roll.
verifier: District emergency management office, fire department, or a community volunteer network running outage and typhoon response
predicate: The household's utility account is a member of the set of accounts flagged by the utility as having medical-equipment dependency (a priority-care roll), without revealing the specific address or usage pattern to every volunteer who handles the list.
disclosed_today: Full address, a copy of the utility bill, the medical certificate or disability card, and a list of equipment, often collected on paper forms and shared with many volunteers.
issuer: Taipower, signing membership in a priority-care or medical-need account list
why_zk: Volunteers and aggregators collect a list of vulnerable people's addresses and bills, which is a safety and privacy risk (it flags who is home, frail, and dependent on power). A membership proof lets a registration desk or a volunteer coordinator check eligibility without holding the dossier. Honest weakness: in an actual emergency the responders genuinely need the address to reach the person, so ZK helps only for the enrollment and eligibility step, not for dispatch; and I am not certain Taipower maintains such a formal roll, so this would depend on the utility creating and signing one.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Proving a single yes/no fact from a signed credential without revealing the underlying record or letting the issuer see where it is used.
The idea that the verifier gets only the attribute the service needs and not the full bill it sits inside.

title: Low-income electricity subsidy proof for school lunch or tuition aid
moment: A parent applies for a school's low-income or near-poor student aid (tuition waiver, free lunch, after-school care subsidy) and is asked to submit a household certificate plus a copy of recent utility bills to show the household sits on the subsidised-electricity roll.
verifier: School administrative office or district education bureau
predicate: The household's electricity account is a member of the utility's low-income or welfare-tariff roll (set membership), with no address or kWh usage revealed.
disclosed_today: Full utility bill with address, account number, meter number, monthly usage and payment history, often photocopied and kept in the student file.
issuer: Taiwan Power Company (Taipower), signing membership of its welfare-tariff roll
why_zk: A signed roll-membership proof gives the school the one fact it needs without the address or usage pattern, which could show when the home is empty. Weakness is that the aid rules usually rest on the household registration and social-affairs certificates, so Taipower's roll is only a secondary or corroborating signal, and the school may legally need the address anyway.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: A proof of a prior check that cannot be linked back to the issuance event or reused to track the holder across verifiers.
Having the utility sign without learning where the credential will later be shown, so the utility cannot link the roll check to the landlord.

title: Water-rate discount roll proof when renting out or switching landlord
moment: A tenant in a subsidised-water or senior/disabled-household rate category moves into a new rental and the new landlord or property manager asks for the previous water or electricity bill to confirm the household qualifies for the shared-meter discount split.
verifier: Landlord or property management company
predicate: The tenant's household is in the water utility's discounted-rate roll (set membership), without disclosing the previous address or consumption.
disclosed_today: Previous water bill showing old address, account holder name, usage volumes, and arrears status.
issuer: Taiwan Water Corporation or Taipei Water Department, signing discount-roll membership
why_zk: The landlord only needs to know the discount applies and so the bill split changes; the old address and usage reveal where the tenant lived and how many people live there. Weakness is that discount rolls are small and the pool of eligible people is tiny, so even a membership proof may be identifying by itself, and a landlord may simply not care enough to adopt a wallet flow.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Checking eligibility separately from the entry so identity is not attached to the draw record.
A single-use unlinkable token that stops double entries without tracking the household.

title: Anonymous eligibility for community solar or energy-saving appliance rebate lottery
moment: A resident enters a local government rebate draw for efficient appliances or a rooftop solar subsidy that is reserved for households on the utility's subsidised or demand-response enrolled roll, and is asked to upload a bill so officials can check enrolment and de-duplicate entries.
verifier: City government bureau running the rebate draw
predicate: The entrant's account is a member of the enrolled subsidy roll and has not already entered (membership plus a single-use token), with no address or usage revealed.
disclosed_today: Bill image with name, address, account number and monthly kWh, stored by the contractor handling the application.
issuer: Taipower, signing enrolment membership of its subsidy or demand-response roll
why_zk: Eligibility and one-entry-per-household can be separated, so the city confirms enrolment and prevents duplicates without learning the address or consumption, much like checking eligibility apart from the ballot. Weakness is that the city usually does need a delivery or installation address after winning, so the proof only protects the entry stage, and a small roll limits the anonymity set.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that collecting a whole bill exceeds the necessary scope of the stated purpose, so the proof should carry only the membership bit.
Choosing what to release at presentation time, here tightened from field selection to a single membership predicate.

title: Taipower subsidy-roll proof for a low-income solar rooftop co-op deposit waiver
moment: A household applies to join a community rooftop-solar or energy-saving appliance trade-in scheme run by a township office or NGO, which offers a reduced deposit or free installation to households on a subsidised electricity roll. The counter asks for a recent Taipower bill photocopy to confirm the discount.
verifier: Township office or NGO running the energy-efficiency program
predicate: This account is a member of the Taipower low-income or vulnerable-household discount roll (set membership, current period)
disclosed_today: Full electricity bill copy showing the service address, account number, monthly kWh usage, billing amounts, and the household name
issuer: Taipower (or the Taipower subsidy roll maintainer, co-signing with the social affairs bureau list)
why_zk: The bill reveals home address and occupancy patterns (usage tells when no one is home), while the scheme only needs yes or no on roll membership. Weakness: the roll is derived from social-welfare status held by local governments, so Taipower may not be the natural signer, and rolls change by period, so freshness and revocation need care. It also needs a nullifier so one account cannot claim twice.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The worry that collected bills are kept under an open-ended exception for the office's own duties, which a proof leaving nothing to retain avoids.
Showing an attribute about a place without revealing the underlying true address, with the holder keeping a lawful-disclosure path for audits.

title: Landlord-free proof that a rented unit is on the residential-rate roll for a tenant subsidy
moment: A tenant applies for a municipal rent subsidy or a student housing grant that requires the unit to be billed at the residential rate (not commercial or illegal sub-divided rates). The office asks for water and electricity bills, which expose the landlord's account, the tenant's name, and the exact unit.
verifier: City housing bureau or university housing office
predicate: The tenant's utility account is a member of the set of accounts on the residential tariff class at an eligible metering configuration (individual meter, not shared)
disclosed_today: Water and electricity bills with full address, landlord or account-holder name, usage, and sometimes unrelated charges
issuer: Taipower and Taiwan Water Corporation (each signs its own roll membership)
why_zk: The office needs only that the unit has its own residential-rate meter, a classic landlord-evasion check, yet collects documents that reveal address and consumption. Honest weakness: the account may be in the landlord's name, so the tenant cannot always obtain a credential, and the office still needs the address to administer the subsidy, so membership alone may not replace address disclosure in the end.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: Handling an identifying wrapper (the account) without exposing the content, with a designated-official exception when disclosure is truly needed.
The failure pattern of demanding a full document copy when no less-intrusive alternative is offered.

title: Disaster-relief priority for households on the medical-equipment power-dependent roll
moment: During a typhoon outage or planned rolling blackout, a household that depends on home ventilators or oxygen concentrators wants priority for restoration or a generator loan from the local fire or health station. Staff ask people to send the address, a medical certificate, and electricity bill by chat or phone.
verifier: District fire department or public health center distributing priority generators
predicate: The account is a member of Taipower's registered power-dependent medical-use customer roll
disclosed_today: Address, diagnosis or medical certificate, bill, and sometimes a photo of the device
issuer: Taipower (maintains the priority-restoration list for medical-equipment households)
why_zk: The responder only needs to know that the household is on the priority roll; diagnosis and usage are sensitive health data that spread across chat groups during emergencies. Weakness: in an emergency the responder usually needs the location to dispatch, so the proof can gate eligibility but cannot replace address sharing, and mobile coverage and wallet access fail during outages. Use it for pre-registration and fair queueing, not dispatch.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The idea that a transaction should release only the one attribute it needs, relying on selective disclosure rather than showing the whole document.
The framing that the legitimate duty is to check eligibility, not to retain a copy of the whole document.

title: Low-income electricity discount without handing over the bill
moment: A household applies to its village/district office or a charity for a summer electricity-cost subsidy or free air-conditioner/appliance replacement programme, and is asked to bring a recent Taipower bill showing the electricity account number, address, usage in kWh and payment history.
verifier: District office or charity running an appliance-replacement or energy-subsidy programme
predicate: The Taipower account is a member of the set of accounts on the current low-income / subsidised-household roll (membership, no address or usage revealed).
disclosed_today: Full electricity bill copy with account number, installation address, monthly kWh usage (which reveals occupancy and habits), billing name and payment record.
issuer: Taipower (or the water/gas utility) signing roll membership for the account
why_zk: A usage history is a rich profile (who is home, when, whether the house is empty), and the office needs only to know the account is on the roll. Weakness: the household often has to be identified anyway for delivery of the appliance or payment of the subsidy, so the proof only helps for the eligibility screening step, and the roll itself is maintained by social-welfare agencies, so the utility signing it needs a data feed that does not exist today.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The warning that a request category can bundle extra data (here contract capacity and address) with the one fact needed, so the request must be narrowed to a single membership claim.

title: Proving a rooftop-solar or farm-pump account is on the registered roll for a grant
moment: A farmer or small household applies for a county subsidy for solar panels, a cold-storage unit or an efficient irrigation pump, and the county office asks for the electricity account's power-contract copy and recent bills to confirm the site is on the registered agricultural or residential-subsidy contract class.
verifier: County agriculture or environment bureau processing the grant
predicate: The electricity account belongs to the set of accounts under the agricultural-use or registered-subsidy contract class (membership, without the account number, location or consumption).
disclosed_today: Contract copy and bills listing account number, exact site address, contract capacity and monthly consumption, which reveal the size and operating pattern of the farm.
issuer: Taipower signing contract-class roll membership for the account
why_zk: Consumption and contract capacity expose business operations and could be used by competitors or for tax scrutiny, while the bureau only needs the class. Weakness: the bureau usually also inspects the site in person and needs the address for the project record, so the proof reduces over-collection at application but not at final approval.

inspired_by.borrowed_aspect: The failure pattern of requiring a full document copy with no less-intrusive alternative stated, here applied to bill copies.
The concern that retained records of who used what become a readable profile, here usage data in filed bill copies.

title: Renter proves tenancy at a utility-registered address to a school or clinic without a bill
moment: A family enrolling a child in a public school catchment, or registering at a community clinic's local-resident programme, is asked for a recent water or electricity bill as proof that they live in a utility-registered dwelling in the district, when they rent and the household registration is elsewhere.
verifier: School administration or local clinic enrolment desk
predicate: The water account belongs to the set of active residential accounts registered within the district catchment (membership in a geographic roll, not the exact address or usage).
disclosed_today: Photocopy of a water or electricity bill showing name, full address, account number, usage and amount owed, which is then filed with the application.
issuer: Taiwan Water Corporation or Taipower signing district-roll membership for the account
why_zk: The verifier needs only that the dwelling is within the catchment, yet keeps a bill copy revealing exact address and consumption, and these copies sit in school files for years. Weakness: schools often legally need the household registration address anyway and may need the exact address for contact, so the membership proof can replace the bill only where the catchment test alone is applied; the account holder may also differ from the tenant.
